acceptance: Every crr-* and pvm-p* item is done, or dropped with the owner's recorded decision
Each of T1 to T5 has a guard that runs in required CI and was shown to fail on a seeded instance of the fault
The outcome snapshot for the whole corpus is committed and matches the rule on develop and on published-results
No platform or matrix name appears in the rule, its labels or its tests
context: Plan and owner decisions for the crr-* and pvm-p* items. Origin: the Polars version-matrix results (2026-11-20, 141 result files) could not enter the corpus; investigation found the cause was general. Two adversarial reviews (2026-11-22) found the first plan would rank nothing and patched one platform; this is the revised plan. The TPC wording is in the blog draft (benchbox-site #239). Interim textcharts graphs were merged in benchbox-site #238 and are removed by #240 at the owner's request: the post uses Results Explorer graphs only.
description:
## Objective
Whether a result is accepted, which ranking it enters, which score it shows and how it is labelled must follow from one rule computed from facts in the result file, the same on every path, on develop, on published-results and in the site. Then publish the Polars version-matrix results through that rule. Closes when every crr-* and pvm-p* item is done.

## Faults being removed
- T1 Outcome keyed on what the writer recorded. Two fields: benchmark.compliance_class, and summary.tpc_metrics (the writer omits Power@Size when it stamps a run non-standard: core/results/schema.py ~1770). Example: three DuckDB TPC-H SF1 query-only results with the same facts; one unstamped is ranked, two stamped unofficial_nonstandard are excluded (R).
- T2 Fact combinations with no outcome. Since #4137 a query-only or throughput-only run cannot be official and no rule says where it goes; the lanes still hold old results.
- T3 Many implementations of the rule (about 40 readers across core, CI, the mirror branch and site TypeScript) that disagree, including four different identity rules.
- T4 Evidence not in the result file: row-count references missing above small scales, stream count read from a configured value, engine that ran not recorded.
- T5 Labels that do not match the fact: passed / not_validated / uncertain for the same fact; embeds without a class label; one label for a default engine that changed.

## Owner decisions (Joe, 2026-11-22; dialogs unless quoted)
1. "rank them with a label": query-only and partial TPC results at a standard scale are ranked in a labelled lane.
2. Public path (submit, publish) accepts them the same as the maintainer path. Subscale stays refused on the public path.
3. Cohort minimum: keep the recorded rule (engine settings and container runs count; versions of one platform do not).
4. Leaderboard shows the newest released version that has a ranked result, as the median of its runs. Development and pre-release builds never stand for the platform. All versions stay in a version view.
5. Results with no per-query row-count evidence stay ranked, labelled "row counts not checked". References are added first for TPC-H, TPC-DS and SSB at the scales that rank.
6. Runs with fewer than three measured iterations are labelled "single iteration" and stay ranked.
7. Benchmarks built with TPC tools (TPC-H Skew, TPC-Havoc, Data Vault, TPC-DS OBT) get the derived label too.
8. "Open local result" keeps showing what the file says, marked "as recorded by the BenchBox version that wrote it, not checked".
9. pvm-d1 is reversed: all three Polars engine settings enter the corpus, published by the maintainer path, not benchbox submit.
10. Polars rerun with three measured iterations. Runs the matrix's swap rule left out of its medians are published.
11. TPC-DS query 41: "This is important. We must identify the true root cause of the row count difference." No fallback publication.
12. Stored DuckDB median files are replaced by their individual runs where every run exists and validates; otherwise kept and labelled. The owner released these 28 paths from the A0 deletion freeze for this purpose (dialog, 2026-11-22: "Release these paths from the freeze and replace them").
13. Serial delivery, one pull request per item. SSB and ClickBench are published first.
14. "I want to use Results Explorer graphs for the blog post not the Textcharts CLI graphs". The post carries no chart until Explorer graphs exist.
15. "we must be address the root cause of these issues not patching only polars".

## Planner decisions (technical; challenge in review, do not silently change)
- The class is derived on read. The writer calls the same function and keeps writing the existing compliance_class vocabulary as information only.
- The score is recomputed from timings for every lane (R: reproduces all 33 ranked TPC power results within 0.1%).
- Stream count comes from throughput stream results, not run.streams.
- Seed is not a class input. Cohorts keyed on seed convention are out of scope (77 of 116 TPC results record none) (R).
- The site derives nothing; the pipeline writes class, lane, label, score and identity into the read model. A read-model version bump lands in the site first.
- A row-count reference above the scales the TPC answer sets cover is agreement with a named reference engine and is labelled as that.
- The variant label keeps coming from the requested engine (execution-variants ADR D8). The observed engine is a separate attribute.

## The rule (facts -> class | public | maintainer | lane | score)
- TPC-H/TPC-DS, standard scale, power + throughput + refresh + stream minimum -> full_spec | yes | yes | combined | QphH/QphDS and Power@Size
- same, power + throughput, no refresh or below stream minimum -> partial | yes | yes | both the power-only and the throughput cohort | from timings
- same, power + refresh, no throughput -> partial | yes | yes | power-only | Power@Size from query timings only (refresh excluded)
- same, power only -> power_only | yes | yes | power-only | Power@Size from timings
- same, throughput only -> throughput_only | yes | yes | throughput | from timings
- TPC-H/TPC-DS below scale 1 -> subscale | no | yes | subscale cohort | Power@Size from timings
- any benchmark, non-standard scale -> nonstandard_scale | yes | yes | none | timings only
- other benchmark, standard scale -> none | yes | yes | its own | its own
- no timed phase (load-only, data-only) -> not a result: not staged, not stored
- TPC-DI -> decided by the TPC-DI admission rule (tpcdi-* items); this rule calls it and does not restate it
- gateway-routed, known defect, failed validation -> unchanged from today
Every ranked TPC row carries "Derived from TPC-H/TPC-DS ... not an official TPC result" plus the class in plain words. Vendor terms, anonymization, tuning and timing coverage stay separate admission checks behind the same entry point; they are not class inputs.

## Tracks and order
A rule and mirror: crr-a0 -> a1 -> a2 -> (a3, a4) -> a5; a6 last.
B Explorer identity and medians: crr-b1 -> b2 (site) -> b3 -> b4 (site) -> b5 (site) -> b6.
C evidence: crr-c1 -> c2; tpcds-expression-q41-row-count-differs-from-sql.
D engine that ran: crr-d1 -> d2.
E Polars: pvm-p1 -> p2 -> p5 (post, site); p3 (TPC-H) -> p6 (post); p4 (TPC-DS, after query 41) -> p7 (post).

## Out of reach
The hosted ingest at api.benchbox.dev is in neither repository. It is out of scope. If it refuses a result the rule admits, or admits one the rule refuses, stop and report to the owner; do not work around it.

## Pull requests
One pull request per item. An item whose change must reach published-results also gets the automatic mirror pull request; that is the same change, not a second item.

## Records touched
Subscale ADR decisions 1 and 5 (superseded), 2-4, 6-7 (extended); methodology ADR answers 2, 3, 9 (amended), 6, 8, 11, 12 (kept); slim-branch ADR (one more vendored file); execution-variants ADR D4 (kept) and D8 (label rule kept; identity amended by crr-b1 to include the comparison version); site validation-admission ADR (amended by crr-c1); results runbook A0 freeze (28 median-file paths released, crr-b6); SEED_CORPUS_SPEC version-matrix folder rule (replaced by a fact-based identity rule); tracker tpc-full-spec-result-schema (amended: stored field informational, no standard-scale result mapped to nonstandard_scale); #4410 compliance snapshot (extended, not duplicated).
